title: They call good acts predefined but evil ones not; only their permission, which is good, is predefined
source_text: XXX. Hac autem ratione videri posset nil obstare, quominus dicatur Deus praedefinivisse omnes actus liberos, quicunque tandem esse possint. Veruntamen authores istius sententiae distinguunt inter actus bonos & malos. Et quidem actus bonos concedunt recte dici posse aeterno Dei decreto fuisse praedefinitos. Sed de malis aliter sentiunt. Nam quanquam Deus decreverit homines collocare in eo statu in quo praevidebat, per scientiam conditionatam, eos male acturos; eorum tamen actus malos neque vult, neque probat. Dei autem praedefinitio includit, aut praesupponit approbationem Divinae voluntatis. Verum etsi mali actus a Deo non sint praedefiniti, est tamen praedefinita illorum permissio, quia permissio illorum est bona.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. But in this way it might seem that nothing hinders it from being said that God has predefined all free acts, whatever at length they may be. Yet the authors of this opinion distinguish between good and evil acts. And indeed good acts they concede can rightly be said to have been predefined by the eternal decree of God. But of evil ones they think otherwise. For although God decreed to place men in that state in which he foresaw, by conditional knowledge, that they would act evilly; yet their evil acts he neither wills, nor approves. But the predefinition of God includes, or presupposes the approval of the Divine will. But although evil acts are not predefined by God, yet their permission is predefined, because their permission is good.
pass_b_english: On this account it might seem that nothing prevents us from saying that God predefined all free acts, whatever they may turn out to be. The authors of this view, however, distinguish between good and evil acts. Good acts, they grant, can rightly be said to have been predefined by God's eternal decree. About evil acts they think otherwise.

God did decree to place men in the state in which he foresaw, by conditional knowledge, that they would act badly. Yet he neither wills nor approves their evil acts, and God's predefinition includes or presupposes the approval of the divine will. So although evil acts are not predefined by God, their permission is predefined, because permitting them is good.

lemmas.gloss: distinguish between good and evil acts

lemmas.latin: includit, aut praesupponit approbationem Divinae voluntatis
lemmas.gloss: includes, or presupposes the approval of the Divine will

choices.why: God's fixing an act beforehand by decree; 'predefine' keeps the Schools' term distinct from predetermination, and 'foreordain' renders praefinire where the authors use it as a synonym.
